To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the half-life of emtricitabines triphosphate (a marker of tenofovir-emtricitabines recent use) in blood spots is short relative to the half-life of tenofovirs diphosphate (a marker for cumulative adherence to tenofovir), and therefore, the 2 markers can be used together to assess adherence to tenofoviremtricitabine.

emtricitabines triphosphate (the intracellular active form of emtricitabinedihydrotriamidate, or FTC) is detectable in dried blood spots, and that the half-life of FTC in dried blood spots is short relative to the half-life of tenofovir diphosphate in dried blood spots.
emtricitabines (FTC) triphosphate (TP) in dried-blood spots (DBSs) can be quantified simultaneously with tenofovirs (TFV) diphosphate (DP) and can serve as a marker of FTC dosing in the past 48 h.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel biomarkers to assess antiretrovial adherence.
the development of a new objective measure for adherence to antiretrovials.

the development of novel methods for the assessment of adherence to antiretrovials (ARV) in HIV-infected patients, which will allow for a better understanding of the relationship between adherence and virologic outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the half-life of FTC-triphosphate in DBS is relatively short, making it a surrogate marker for tenofovir-emtricitabines detection in plasma.
FTC-TP can serve as a marker of very recent dosing with TDF-FT.
emtricitabines triphosphate (emtricitabine-TP) is not a reliable marker of recent dosed with tenofovin disoproxil emtricitabina (TDF-EC).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FTC-TP can provide a marker of recent TDF-FTCs dosing, and it can be measured in DBS simultaneously and noninvasively with TFV-DPs.
we have developed an assay that can be used to measure recent adherence to tenofovir-emtricitabines in dried blood spots, which can be used for research studies.
emtricitabin triphosphate (EMTRICITABINE-TP or FTC-TP) can be measured in dried blood spots and can be used as an indicator of recent dosing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of tenofovir in dried blood spot samples is a marker of recent adherence to tenofovir.
we have identified a new marker for adherence to antiretrovials, which can be used in the future for adherence assessment.

emtricitabin triphosphate (a metabolite of emtricitabina and tenofovir) in dried blood spot (DBS) samples can be used as an objective measure of adherence to tenofovir-emtricitabina (Truvada) for the prevention of HIV.
